title: Record the user's prompt as open work on the session record
action: A session that never calls a bee flow verb — a plain question, a bee-researching run — leaves no record of WHAT it was asked to do, so a dashboard reading .bee/sessions/<id>.json can say the session is working but not on what. Close that. On UserPromptSubmit, hook activity writes a `work` object beside `activity` on the same record: {title, text, status, opened_at, updated_at, turns}. D1: status starts "open" and this cell writes no other value — moving it is the agent's job in a later slice. D3: the FIRST prompt's text becomes `title` and never changes while the record is open; a follow-up prompt appends to `text` and bumps turns/updated_at instead of opening a second record. D5: `text` keeps the user's wording, but absolute paths are scrubbed and a secret-shaped prompt is stored as "[redacted]" — reuse SECRET_PATTERNS from verbs/decisions/scanners.rs (private key, AKIA, ghp, sk-, JWT, key=value) and ONLY that half: assert_safe_content also runs INJECTION_PATTERNS ("ignore previous instructions"), which a user types legitimately every day and which must NOT redact ordinary work. TWO PLACEMENT RULES, both load-bearing. First: the prompt write happens BEFORE the state machine's suppression and no-transition early returns in record_activity — a prompt arriving is a fact about the session no matter what the state machine concludes, and routing it through the transition logic drops prompts whenever the prior state was sticky (blocked, waiting_input). Second: both sinks, same as the state — a herded pane has no session record, only .bee/mailbox/<job-id>/activity.json through write_activity_herded, and the work object goes there too. Keep the hook's posture exactly: never deny, never print on stdout, always exit 0, every failure swallowed into the crash log. D4 needs NO code — the record hangs off the session file and every reader already drops a session whose last_heartbeat is stale; prove that with a test rather than building an expiry.

truths: A UserPromptSubmit event writes work{title,text,status:open,opened_at,updated_at,turns} on the session record
The first prompt's text is the title and stays the title across follow-up prompts, which append to text and bump turns
An absolute path in the prompt does not reach the stored text
Each of the six SECRET_PATTERNS shapes redacts the prompt to [redacted]
An injection-shaped prompt is stored normally, never redacted
A prompt arriving while the prior state is sticky (blocked or waiting_input) is still recorded
A herded pane records the work object into its job mailbox, not a session file
The hook still exits 0 and prints nothing on stdout on every failure path

Folded the work write into the existing activity write rather than adding a second lock acquisition ahead of the state machine early-returns, as plan.md described. UserPromptSubmit maps to working and is a turn boundary, so it provably reaches the write past both the no-transition return and the sticky suppression; a second acquire_store_lock_once could silently drop a prompt on a busy lock, which is worse than the case the ordering rule guarded. The invariant is pinned by a test that fires a prompt while the prior state is blocked
